stem: A clinical photograph shows the breast of a 45-year-old non-lactating woman: it is diffusely erythematous, warm and oedematous with prominent 'peau d'orange' skin over more than a third of the breast, but no discrete lump is palpable. There has been no response to a course of antibiotics. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: A rapidly progressive, warm, erythematous, oedematous breast with peau d'orange affecting a large area, no discrete mass and no response to antibiotics in a non-lactating woman is inflammatory breast carcinoma (T4d), due to tumour emboli obstructing dermal lymphatics. It is aggressive and needs urgent biopsy, not further antibiotics; true mastitis/abscess occurs typically during lactation and responds to treatment.
subject: Surgery
